- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer to lower end of forecast range.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward MA by 2–4% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit recent trend; dampen forecast slope by 10–15% for 10+ consecutive days of sentiment volatility.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2) within 3 days, model often fails to anticipate sharp drop; reduce forecast by 5–8% for next 3 days.
